prompt: All circles x²+y²+2λx+c=0 (c fixed, λ varies) have common radical axis…
explain: Subtracting two members gives 2(λ₁−λ₂)x=0, so x=0, the y-axis.
subject: Mathematics
topic: Family of circles and radical axis

prompt: Radius of the circle with centre at origin touching the line 3x + 4y = 10 is:
explain: Radius = distance from centre to the line = 10/√(9+16) = 2.
subject: Mathematics
topic: Standard form of equation of circle

prompt: Line lx+my+n=0 bisects the circumference of x²+y²+2gx+2fy+c=0 iff?
explain: It must pass through the centre (−g,−f): −lg−mf+n=0, so lg+mf=n.
subject: Mathematics

prompt: Reflecting x²+y²+2gx+2fy+c=0 in the x-axis changes which constant?
explain: Centre (−g,−f) goes to (−g,f) and the radius is unchanged, so only f changes sign.
subject: Mathematics

prompt: Circle has diameter AB. Power of any point P w.r.t. it equals?
explain: The expression is (P−A)·(P−B), and it equals S₁, the power of P.
subject: Mathematics

prompt: Least distance of an external point P from a circle with centre C and radius r is?
explain: The nearest point lies on line CP, so the least distance is CP − r. √(CP² − r²) is the tangent length.
subject: Mathematics
topic: Position of a point w.r.t. circle

prompt: For the circle written as −x²−y²+9=0, a point inside the circle makes the LHS?
explain: The sign rule S₁ < 0 holds only when the x² coefficient is positive. With −x²−y²+9, the origin gives +9, which is positive.
subject: Mathematics
topic: Position of a point w.r.t. circle

prompt: Minimum area of the triangle cut from the axes by a tangent to x²+y²=a² is:
explain: 1/a² = 1/p²+1/q² ≥ 2/|pq| gives |pq| ≥ 2a², so area ½|pq| ≥ a².
subject: Mathematics

prompt: Tangents to (x−h)²+(y−k)²=r² parallel to the x-axis are:
explain: The horizontal tangents lie at distance r above and below the centre.
subject: Mathematics

prompt: Locus of P from which tangents to x²+y²=a² are inclined at 60°:
explain: OP = a/sin30° = 2a, so P lies on x²+y² = 4a².
subject: Mathematics

prompt: Tangent y = mx + c to x²+y²=a² with m>0, c>0 touches the circle in which quadrant?
explain: Contact point (−mc/(1+m²), c/(1+m²)) has x<0, y>0.
subject: Mathematics

prompt: Locus of centre of a circle of radius r touching the line ax+by+c=0:
options: Two lines parallel to it at distance r
One line parallel to it at distance r
explain: Centre is at distance r from the line, so it lies on either of two parallels at distance r.
subject: Mathematics

prompt: Locus of centre of a circle touching two given intersecting lines is:
options: Pair of angle bisectors of the lines
Circle through their point of intersection
explain: Equal distances from both lines give both internal and external angle bisectors.
subject: Mathematics

prompt: Number of circles touching all three sides (lines) of a triangle:
explain: One incircle and three excircles.
subject: Mathematics

prompt: Points of contact of two parallel tangents to a circle are:
options: Ends of a diameter perpendicular to the tangents
Ends of a diameter parallel to the tangents
Ends of a chord not through the centre
Two points on the same radius
explain: Radii to the contact points are ⟂ to the tangents, so both lie on one diameter, diametrically opposite.
subject: Mathematics

prompt: A circle is centred at the radical centre of three circles, with radius equal to its tangent length. It cuts them:
explain: Its radius equals the tangent length from its centre to each circle, which is the condition for orthogonality.
subject: Mathematics

prompt: Locus of P with (tangent length to S₁)² − (tangent length to S₂)² = k, k ≠ 0 constant, is a:
options: Line parallel to the radical axis
Line perpendicular to the radical axis
Circle coaxal with S₁ and S₂
explain: x²+y² terms cancel, leaving a linear equation differing from S₁−S₂=0 only in the constant term.
subject: Mathematics
topic: Length of tangent, power of a point

prompt: P is at distance d from the centre of a circle of radius r. Its power w.r.t. the circle is?
explain: Power = PC² − r²; it is negative inside the circle and equals (tangent length)² outside.

prompt: Tangent length from P to x²+y²=r² equals r. Distance OP from the centre is?
explain: OP² = r² + PT² = 2r², so OP = r√2.
subject: Mathematics
topic: Length of tangent, power of a point

prompt: Tangents from P to a circle are perpendicular. Chord of contact subtends what angle at the centre?
explain: Centre, two contact points and P form a square, so the angle at the centre is 180°−90° = 90°.
subject: Mathematics
topic: Chord of contact and pair of tangents

prompt: Chord of contact from the origin to x²+y²+2gx+2fy+c=0 (c>0) is?
explain: Put (x₁,y₁)=(0,0) in T=0: g·x + f·y + c = 0.
subject: Mathematics
topic: Chord of contact and pair of tangents

prompt: Two concentric circles have unequal radii. Number of common tangents?
explain: The smaller circle lies strictly inside the larger, so no common tangent exists.
subject: Mathematics

prompt: Two circles intersect at two points. Number of transverse (internal) common tangents?
explain: Only the 2 direct common tangents exist; transverse ones need d ≥ r₁+r₂.
subject: Mathematics

prompt: The length √(d² − (r₁−r₂)²) of the direct common tangent becomes zero when the circles:
explain: d = |r₁−r₂| is the internal touching condition, so the tangent length shrinks to zero.
subject: Mathematics

prompt: Circles are drawn on the three sides of a triangle as diameters. Their radical centre is the:
explain: Each pair of circles meets at a foot of an altitude, so the radical axes are the altitudes.
subject: Mathematics

prompt: For two intersecting circles, the longest possible common chord has length equal to:
explain: The chord is at most the smaller circle's diameter, attained when it passes through the smaller circle's centre.
subject: Mathematics

prompt: Circles of equal radii touch two given equal circles externally. Their centre lies on:
options: Perpendicular bisector of the join of centres
explain: The distances to both centres equal r + ρ, so the point is equidistant from the two centres.
subject: Mathematics

prompt: Angle of intersection of two touching circles is:
explain: Both circles have the same tangent at the point of contact, so the angle between them is 0.
subject: Mathematics

prompt: Before subtracting to get a radical axis, circle equations must first be written with:
options: x² and y² coefficients equal to 1
explain: Dividing by the leading coefficient makes the second-degree terms cancel on subtraction.
subject: Mathematics

prompt: Circles x²+y²−2x=0 and x²+y²+2x=0 are in which position?
explain: Centres (±1,0), radii 1, so d = 2 = r₁ + r₂.
subject: Mathematics

prompt: Circles x²+y²=1 and (x−1)²+(y−1)²=1 are in which position?
explain: d = √2, and |r₁−r₂| = 0 < √2 < 2 = r₁+r₂.
subject: Mathematics

prompt: Circles of radii 4 and 9 touch externally. Length of a direct common tangent?
subject: Mathematics

prompt: Circles x²+y²=4 and x²+y²−6x−8y+21=0 have how many common tangents?
explain: Centres (0,0), (3,4): d=5; radii 2 and 2; d > 4 = r₁+r₂, so the circles are separate and have 4 tangents.
subject: Mathematics

prompt: Two circles touch externally. Their common tangent at the point of contact is a:
options: Radical axis of a coaxal limiting pair
explain: The circles lie on opposite sides of this tangent, so it is transverse; the other two are direct.
subject: Mathematics

prompt: Number of common tangents to x²+y²=9 and x²+y²−8x+7=0?
explain: Centres (0,0),(4,0), r=3,3; d=4 lies between 0 and 6, so the circles intersect: 2 tangents.
subject: Mathematics

prompt: A coaxal system with real, distinct limiting points consists of which type of circles?
explain: Intersecting coaxal systems have no real limiting points. Non-intersecting systems have two.
subject: Mathematics

prompt: Two non-concentric circles of equal radii have a radical axis that is which line?
options: A common tangent of the circles
Perpendicular bisector of the line of centres
explain: Equal radii give equal power at the midpoint of the centres, and the axis is perpendicular to the line of centres.
subject: Mathematics

explain: Points on the axis have equal power, positive for non-intersecting circles, so they lie outside both circles.
